title: Boards under Leibniz's rule
claim: With the board made of identity distinctions on the words of F2 and a finitary value law over a finite alphabet, Leibniz's rule (names u and v are one place iff s(ug) = s(vg) for every word g) makes the boards exactly the Schreier graphs Sch(Stab(s)) of the solutions s on the tree (T1). Proved: the strong form S (every board the tree or finite) is false, since the horofunction law on Z/3 has the board Sch(<x^3>) (T2); Lemma A, a periodic solution using a branching pattern gives a solution with trivial stabilizer and one with an infinite cyclic stabilizer (T3); Lemma B, without a solution of trivial stabilizer some open set of solutions is fixed by an h != 1, rigid off h's axis, finite and isolated (T4); the dichotomy W (an infinite board brings the tree) and P (no law makes every board quadratic) for deterministic laws and for laws with a periodic branching solution, which by ticket B covers all 1,024 Life-like one-bit laws and the atom (T5, T6). Not proved: W in general; it is reduced to excluding a non-isolated solution fixed by some h != 1, rigid away from one end of h's axis, whose far alternative completions are all isolated.
failure_conditions: A law with an infinite board under Leibniz's rule and no board on the tree (W).
A law whose every board under Leibniz's rule grows quadratically (P).
A periodic solution with a branching pattern and no solution with trivial stabilizer (T3).
foundation_claim_scope: Boards made of identity distinctions on the names of the free group on two letters, under Leibniz's rule in full; finitary value laws over finite alphabets. Identity distinctions are distinctions of the law, never contact (A51).

validation.independence: Written by Claude in one session at the coordinator's go-ahead on 2026-11-10 (sub-goal B111).
validation.status: proved by hand; finite checks in check.py passed (result.json); the general W reduced, not proved
validation.novelty: T2 to T4 elementary and close to folklore (Busemann functions, Baire category); W not found stated for free groups (bounded search 2026-11-10; Piantadosi 2008 and Bitar, arXiv 2406.04132, treat the converse direction and stabilizer families).
